correctness.rationale: The second component forces a primitive orbit to alternate (p,q) and (q,p), with p≠q. Subtraction of the two update equations fixes p+q=(1+a−v)/u; addition fixes the product as [uS²+(v+a−1)S+2d]/(2u). Their discriminant is the claimed Δ, and the sum and the difference reconstruct both updates, so Δ>0 is necessary and sufficient and gives one unordered orbit. The two alternating derivatives have trace of their product a²+f′(p)+f′(q)=1+(1+a)² and product determinant (1+a)²−u²(p−q)². Hence the characteristic polynomial is negative at 1 and (1+a)², has two distinct real roots, and its sign at −1 is the sign of H−K. This gives the stated three regions, using hyperbolicity for endomorphisms even if the contracting multiplier vanishes, and instability also in the nonhyperbolic case. Even if attraction is taken to mean convergence without Lyapunov stability, a small closed ball in eigen-coordinates of the return map has a nowhere dense trapped set: differences initially along the expanding direction stay in an expanding cone while both trajectories stay there, since μ+>max(1,|μ−|). The determinant of the return derivative is the nonzero polynomial f′(r)f′(s), so the return map is locally open on a dense set; preimages of those closed nowhere dense trapped sets are nowhere dense. A countable union of such preimages for both phases cannot fill a neighborhood. The invertible map (x,y)↦(ax+3y/2,x) gives the specialization with u=−3b/2; K factors as (c−1−a)(c−1+3a), giving both bounds and the orbit formula. An independent exact replay checked six prescribed cycles (including a zero multiplier and −1 boundary) and recomputed in the original coordinates the rational witness (4/79,−14/395) ↔ (−5/79,2/79), whose return polynomial is λ²−41λ/25+6319/10000.
residual_risks: The count is for primitive period two over the reals only. A multiplier −1 is not by itself a higher-period bifurcation claim. No global basin classification or conclusions for u=0 are implied.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exhaustive signed-parameter real cycle and stability classification rather than a single simulation. Its universal expanding direction settles whether an apparently stable period-two branch can be a full-plane attractor; the exact witness and analysis arbitrarily close to the flip give an actionable correction. The exact −1 boundary further distinguishes saddles from repellers.
